title: Mountain Peaks
statement: Heights along a hiking trail are given in an array. A peak is a point that is strictly higher than both of its neighbours; the first and last points are never peaks. Return the number of peaks.

examples.explanation: 4 is a peak; the two 5s are equal, so neither is strictly higher than both neighbours.

answerKey.pattern: Single scan comparing each inner point with its two neighbours
keyPoints: Loop from the second point to the second-to-last point
Count a point when it is strictly greater than the point before and the point after
edgeCases: The first and last points are never peaks

hints: Which positions can never be a peak?
Each inner point only needs its left and right neighbour.
Use strict comparisons so that flat tops are not counted.
